top.title: How Micah Ford flipped ignominious era for Stanford football into his personal legacy
top.description: Micah Ford #20 of the Stanford Cardinal looks on before a game against the Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets on Sept. 26, 2026 at Stanford Stadium in Palo Alto, Calif. (Matthew Huang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) Micah Ford has witnessed the lows of this Stanford football era. In November 2024, as a freshman, he watched from the California Memorial Stadium sideline as quarterback Fernando Mendoza went "98 yards with my boys" to lead an epic Big Game comeback, handing Stanford its first four-game losing streak against Cal since 2005. He was in the building four months later, when recently hired general manager Andrew Luck fired Troy Taylor, the head coach who had recruited him, citing the need for a "reset" after an investigation concluded that Taylor had bullied and belittled female staffers. Ford saw all of it. The 3-9 season in 2024. The 4-8 campaign a year ago. The slow start this season. He played for one head coach as a freshman (Taylor), then another as a sophomore (interim Frank Reich), and now another as a junior playing for first-year head coach Tavita Pritchard. Chaos and turmoil were all he knew. Midway through October, the feeling couldn't have been much better. The Cardinal were 2-4, and each blowout loss looked worse than the last. His team lost those games by a combined 172 points. Ford, the engine of the offense at running back, wasn't producing. But after that 58-7 loss to then-No. 6 Notre Dame on Oct. 10, something changed. Stanford, led by Ford's sudden emergence, became an unrecognizable football team. The first six games of Ford's season: 95 carries, 350 yards (3.7 yards per carry) and four rushing touchdowns. The last five: 108 carries, 701 yards (6.5 YPC) and nine rushing touchdowns. His yardage totals, including receptions, in each of those games were 231, 208, 120, 150 and 156. He's been the most consistent presence for an offense that desperately needed it under fourth-year running backs coach Malcolm Agnew. Ford's success directly led to Stanford's (6-5, 4-4 ACC) success. The Cardinal have won four of their last five games. They destroyed Cal 44-28 in Saturday's Big Game and earned bowl-game eligibility for the first time since 2018. Looking back, Ford can easily say it was all worth it. "To be at a program where, obviously, I didn't have success early, and then to see it gel into the program that we knew it could be," Ford said Saturday, "it's kind of just, like, I'm at a loss of words for it. "Honestly, there was no way we were leaving without that axe today," he added, after rushing for 151 yards and two touchdowns. "I don't know how long (it's been since) Stanford kept it two years in a row. It's probably been a little while." Ford is correct. The last time Stanford won consecutive games against Cal was in 2018, the last of a dominant nine-year Big Game run. Following that season, the Bears won five of six matchups from 2019-2024. top.description: Kansas City quarterback Patrick Mahomes, left, and Buffalo quarterback Josh Allen, right, will lead their clubs into an NFL Thanksgiving holiday showdown with the best record in the NFL's American Conference up for grabs (David Eulitt) Kansas City quarterback Patrick Mahomes and Buffalo superstar Josh Allen face a Thursday showdown on the US Thanksgiving holiday that will have a major impact on the NFL playoff picture. The Bills own the AFC's best record at 9-1 and beating the Chiefs (8-2) would help ensure a home-field edge in the post-season. "We know what type of team they are," Allen said. It's always exciting. It's always fun." The Bills have averaged 31 points in their win streak while the Chiefs have won three in a row with 34 or more points each game. This dreary dystopian cyberpunk realm originates from sci-fi legend Phillip K. Dick's 1968 novel, "Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?," and was then so vividly brought to life in Ridley Scott’s seminal 1982 adaptation, " Blade Runner ." The 2017 sequel, "Blade Runner 2049," was directed by "Arrival’s" and "Dune’s" Denis Villeneuve. Starring Michelle Yeoh, Hunter Schafer, Matthew Needham, Dimitri Abold, and Lewis Gribben, " Blade Runner 2099 " hails from creator and showrunner Silka Louisa and Alcon Entertainment founders Andrew Kosove and Broderick Johnson, who executive produce with Ridley Scott's Scott Free Productions. top.title: Paul Pierce Admits 2013 Trade Built Current Celtics Core
top.description: Neville E. Guard-Imagn Images The Boston Celtics won the 2024 NBA title, but the foundation was laid when the franchise traded away its biggest star. Paul Pierce, the man who led the team to victory in 2008, says he has zero regrets about leaving in 2013. He knows the picks Boston received from that deal turned into the two players who finally brought the trophy back. The Trade That Changed Everything Back in 2013, the Brooklyn Nets were desperate and desperate teams make mistakes. They traded for Pierce and Kevin Garnett, giving up three unprotected first-round picks and a pick swap. The Nets project failed hard, and the assets Boston got in return became the keys to the kingdom. According to HITC , Pierce told the Amongst Legends podcast that the trade was handled with total transparency. He respected the process even though it meant leaving Boston. When the Nets finished with a 21-61 record in 2016, Boston used the number three overall pick to draft Jaylen Brown. The next year, the Celtics exercised their pick swap after Brooklyn had the worst record in the league. In the 2017 Draft, Danny Ainge traded down to let the Sixers select Markelle Fultz while the Lakers chose Lonzo Ball. Boston then swooped in to select Jayson Tatum with the third pick. Those two young stars led the team to a championship in 2024, defeating the Mavericks in the Finals. Pierce Owns The Legacy Many fans might think trading Pierce was a mistake, but he sees it differently now. He says the current success of the franchise rests on the foundation his departure created. A Look Back at California Roots Conner Henry, a native of Claremont, California, is part of that long history. He was selected by the Houston Rockets in the 1988 NBA Draft, but he had signed with Boston in 1987. His time with the team was short, lasting only until he was cut that fall. During his stay, Henry averaged 2.7 points per game. AOL.com notes that the Celtics have sought talent from nearly every U.S. state since their early days.

top.title: Cleveland Guardians Add Lefty Starter on $17.5 Million Deal
top.description: Oct 12, 2026; Milwaukee, Wisconsin, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Kris Bubic (40) throws a pitch against the Milwaukee Brewers during the fifth inning in game two of the NLCS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at American Family Field. Mandatory Credit: Michael McLoone-Imagn Images The Cleveland Guardians made their first significant free-agent addition of the winter on Tuesday, agreeing to terms with left-hander Kris Bubic on a one-year, $17.5 million contract, according to multiple reports. The deal, which is pending a physical, is the largest one-year guarantee in franchise history and gives Cleveland a familiar AL Central arm to bolster a rotation that already features Parker Messick and Gavin Williams. Bubic, 29, was a 2025 American League All-Star with the Royals, posting a career-best 2.55 ERA over 116⅓ innings that season. His 2026 campaign was far more limited. Elbow and shoulder issues sidelined him for much of the year; he finished with a 3.76 ERA across 55 innings split between Kansas City and the Dodgers after a deadline trade. When healthy, he has shown a five-pitch mix built around a rising four-seam fastball, a firm changeup, and a pair of breaking balls, along with a delivery that has historically generated soft contact and ground balls. For Cleveland, the signing fits a clear priority. The Guardians entered the offseason looking to add starting pitching depth after a season in which they were the only team in baseball to have four pitchers make at least 30 starts. Bubic is expected to slot into the middle of a group that also includes Messick (2026 AL Rookie of the Year and Cy Young finalist), Williams (AL strikeout leader), Tanner Bibee, and several depth options. Outside the Bubic agreement, Cleveland’s offseason activity has been quiet and roster-focused. At the non-tender deadline, they non-tendered utility man David Fry, agreed to deals with relievers Matt Festa and Colin Holderman plus outfielder Blake Perkins to avoid arbitration, and have signed minor-league free agents (including right-hander Jairo Iriarte and left-hander Antoine Kelly). They also added several players to the 40-man roster and claimed José Tena off waivers. With the collective bargaining agreement set to expire December 1, the remaining window for additional moves is short . Bubic gives the Guardians an upside left-handed starter on a prove-it deal while they evaluate further pitching or lineup needs.

top.title: NFL Clears DK Metcalf Of Suspension After Sunday Ejection
top.description: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images The National Football League has decided against suspending Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf after he was ejected during Sunday’s loss to the Philadelphia Eagles. This ruling comes despite Metcalf committing two unsportsmanlike conduct penalties that led to his removal from the game late in the third quarter. The league determined that a suspension was not warranted for the incident where Metcalf allegedly tried to poke Eagles cornerback Cooper DeJean in the eye. While the suspension is off the table, the league will still review the conduct to see if a fine is necessary. Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy addressed the situation during his Monday media availability, noting that he and Metcalf had spoken about the event. McCarthy described the conversations between the two as “productive” and stated that any further discipline from the team would be kept internal. “Life’s about learning situations,” McCarthy said. He also expressed his belief in second chances, noting that he would judge Metcalf based on their personal interactions rather than just the penalty flags. A History of Discipline This ejection marks the third time in his eight-season career that Metcalf has been thrown out of a game. The final two games of the 2025 regular season carry a suspension for the player due to behavior stemming from a physical altercation with a Lions fan in Detroit. The financial toll on the player has been significant, with his fines totaling a whopping $245,647 according to reports. This total excludes an extra $555,555 fine associated with the two-game suspension resulting from the Lions fan altercation. After Sunday’s game, Metcalf exited the locker room without talking to reporters, though he came back to speak with the media on Monday. ProFootballTalk states that he rejected claims he intended to poke Cooper DeJean in the eye. With just one catch on four targets for two yards before ejection, the 28-year-old receiver struggled to find his rhythm this season. In 10 games, the two-time Pro Bowler has secured 36 of his 74 targets, accumulating 434 yards and only two touchdowns. Looking Ahead to Denver Metcalf remains on the Steelers’ active roster as they prepare for their next matchup. The team has a short week to recover before hosting the Denver Broncos at Acrisure Stadium. The game is scheduled for Friday, Nov. 27, with kickoff set for 3 p.m. ET. top.title: Dyson Daniels Proves The League Wrong On Value
top.description: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images Dyson Daniels is the Atlanta Hawks’ most valuable player, not Jalen Johnson, because he drives wins without shooting. Soaring Down South reported that Daniels holds a staggering +18.0 on/off net rating to start the year. This number is the best on the team. The league thinks a shooter is needed to win. Daniels is changing that view with his defense and speed. He impacts winning in every way except shooting, which is a rare skill set. The Thompson twins are the only other players who succeed this way, but both are struggling this season. Amen Thompson has a -9.7 on/off rating with the Rockets, while Ausar sits at +2.2 with the Pistons. Daniels has surpassed both of them. A Deal That Saves The Hawks Money Daniels remains on a team-friendly deal of $25 million per year through the 2029-2030 season. He will have the 35th-highest salary in the league that year, making it the 23rd-lowest contract. Other players in his $20-30 million range include Damian Lillard, Herb Jones, and PJ Washington. Daniels is only 23 years old, one year younger than Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg. By the time his contract ends after the 2030 season, he will be 27 and entering his prime. The contract gives the Hawks an advantage over other teams.

top.title: Mahomes And Reid Show Chiefs Pride Supports Kansas City Current
top.description: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images The Kansas City Chiefs did not wait for a press release to show support for their city. Patrick Mahomes and Andy Reid made their stance clear on Sunday at Arrowhead Stadium. While the team prepared for a matchup against the Arizona Cardinals, the focus shifted to a family moment that celebrated a local soccer title. Mahomes, dressed in his full uniform, stopped to greet his wife and children. This act of love happened right before kickoff on a cold November afternoon. A Family Moment on the Sideline The video of the reunion spread fast across social media after the league shared it. Mahomes was already in his red No. 15 jersey when he walked over to the sideline. His children were bundled up in warm coats against the chill. One daughter wore a pale pink puffer coat while the other stood close. The quarterback bent down to wrap his arms around both kids for hugs and kisses. He then turned his attention to Brittany Mahomes, who wore a long black coat. She reached up to touch his face before they shared a kiss. The NFL posted the clip on X with a simple note about the moment. They wrote, “@PatrickMahomes getting some pregame love from his favorite people,” according to Sports Illustrated . Fans React to the Tribute Local fans saw the connection between the NFL champion and the NWSL champions immediately. Brittany Mahomes had already shared photos of the Kansas City Current winning their title. Her husband and the head coach supported her, and the community took notice. People watching the feed reacted with warm words about the scene. One person commented, “Okay that hug actually got me,” per Sports Illustrated. Another viewer simply said, “They are adorable.” A third fan summed up the feeling of the day by writing, “pregame with the family hits different.” These comments show how much the city cares about all its teams, not just one. The Chiefs have built a culture that values family and local pride in equal measure. Mahomes and Reid proved that point without saying a word during the game. The team won their match against Arizona with a final score of 34 to 7 on Sunday. Now the squad looks ahead to their next challenge on the road. The Kansas City Chiefs will play the Buffalo Bills on Thursday, Nov. 26, at 8:20 p.m.

top.title: Lakers Target P.J. Washington To Strengthen Frontcourt
top.description: David Richard-Imagn Images The Los Angeles Lakers are making moves to fix their frontcourt before the trade deadline arrives. General manager Rob Pelinka wants to shore up the team’s depth and add a reliable wing player. Reports indicate the club is targeting Dallas Mavericks forward P.J. Washington to fill a specific hole in their rotation. Heavy.com outlines a specific plan where Dallas sends Washington to Los Angeles in exchange for Jarred Vanderbilt, Jaden Hardy, and two future second-round picks. The Mavericks would receive the picks to add assets to their roster while clearing space for other players. This move would reunite Washington with Luka Doncic, his former teammate from Dallas. The Lakers see Washington as the missing piece to help their star trio dominate the playoffs. Why The Lakers Need Washington Los Angeles has struggled to find a consistent two-way player at the forward spot this season. The team needs someone who can guard top scorers and hit open shots without needing the ball. Heavy.com notes that Washington fits this exact profile. Washington is putting up solid numbers this year. While shooting 36.2% from three-point range, he averages 14.0 points, 6.7 rebounds, and 1.3 assists. Those stats show he can contribute immediately without disrupting the flow of the offense. The Lakers have been linked to him for a long time, but the salary cap makes it difficult. His $88 million contract is a big hurdle, yet the front office seems willing to take the risk. Backup Center Search Continues While chasing Washington, the Lakers are also looking for a backup center to play behind Walker Kessler. Marc Stein reported Sunday that the team is actively seeking help in the middle. “Lakers have been actively searching for another center to play behind Walker Kessler and general manager Rob Pelinka has all but promised that a move is forthcoming to address that need,” Stein wrote. The team has limited draft capital to use as leverage in these talks. One potential target is Mavericks center Moussa Cissé. Rookie guard Walter Clayton Jr. could be added to Dallas’s roster, which might require moving Cissé, and Stein noted that the Lakers have only three tradeable second‑round picks, highlighting their limited draft capital, though Los Angeles could trade Kevon Looney and a pick for Cissé despite the 24‑year‑old logging just 36 minutes this season. He is a gamble on upside rather than a sure thing. The Trade Deadline Approach Rob Pelinka has made it clear that the team plans to be active before the deadline. He spoke on Spectrum SportsNet about the need to fix issues the team has spotted. “We’ll be active at the trade deadline to shore up things that we see,” Pelinka said during a Spectrum SportsNet interview. The front office knows the roster has gaps that need filling if they want to challenge for a championship.

top.description: Czech No 1 Jiri Lehecka beat Felix Auger-Aliassime 7-6(4) 6-2 to seal a 2-0 quarter-final victory for Czechia over Canada in the Davis Cup . The world No 14’s victory ensured Czechia booked their place in the last four of tennis’ ‘World Cup’ for the first time in more than a decade. Earlier on Tuesday Tomas Mahac beat Liam Draxl 6-2 3-6 6-2 to put the Czechs in front, with Lehecka’s straightforward win meaning there was no need for the dead-rubber doubles match to be played, with Davis Cup ties best of three. Czechia will now play either three-time defending champions Italy, led by Flavio Cobolli, or South Korea, who face off on Wednesday. The semi-final will take place on Friday. Auger-Aliassime, a former world No 4 now ranked 17th, squandered ​nine ⁠break points, including a set ‌point at 5-4 in the opening set, before Lehecka forced a tiebreak. Lehecka said: “It was a super tough match. I was forced to play very well facing some break points and some tough situations. “Felix is such a dangerous player in these conditions, so I’m very proud with the way I converted the chances I had in the first set and also how I was able to improve my game in the second. top.title: Guirassy makes bold claim about his place among world's best strikers
top.description: Guirassy makes bold claim about his place among world's best strikers Borussia Dortmund striker Serhou Guirassy believes he belongs among the world's top five forwards and has not ruled out winning the Ballon d'Or . In an interview with “ Bild” , the 30-year-old also opened up about his relationship with Fábio Silva and his future at the Bundesliga club. Asked whether he receives enough recognition, Guirassy made a confident assessment of his position in world football. "If you look at the last three or four years, there are strikers like Kane and Mbappé – and I would say that I might be fourth or fifth ," he explained. The Dortmund forward also believes the Ballon d'Or is within reach, despite finishing 21st in the 2025 voting. "Anything is possible for anyone – including me. For me, football is always about the moment," Guirassy said. "If you have a great season with your team, anything can happen." One of the keys to Dortmund's success could be the partnership between Guirassy and Fábio Silva. The Guinea international insists there is no rivalry between the two forwards. "He is like my little brother. I don't see Fábio as competition. My competition is myself. I want to be better every day than I was the day before," he said. Guirassy also praised Silva's versatility, adding that the pair have shown they can play together and support each other. Finally, the 30-year-old addressed speculation about his long-term future. His current contract runs until 2028, but an extension is certainly something he could imagine. "There was a period when I wasn't happy. Today, I am very happy. And fundamentally, I can imagine it " , Guirassy revealed. "Dortmund are a top club. I want to win something here and I feel comfortable."

top.title: Jets Win Proves Geno Smith Deserves A Return Contract

The offense moved the ball with a balance the team has not seen in years. This game proves the Jets can win even when the defense struggles. ESPN’s Rich Cimini noted that this was Smith’s fourth game with three touchdown passes and an 80 percent completion rate. The team should not look to replace him in 2027. Aaron Glenn Sees Real Progress Head coach Aaron Glenn praised the offensive unit after the game. He told reporters, “We did a really good job of being balanced, scoring in the red zone.” Glenn also highlighted how well the team used its playmakers. I’m glad we have him.” Rookie David Bailey also made his mark with two more sacks, bringing his season total to 9.5. He is on pace to break a rookie sack record set nearly 30 years ago. nigeria.title: Campaign violence: INEC awaits police case files to prosecute offenders
nigeria.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Independent National Electoral Commission INEC has asked the Nigeria Police Force to speed up the arrest, investigation and transmission of case files against perpetrators of campaign violence, so the Commission can prosecute them directly. The INEC Chairman, Professor Joash Amupitan SAN, said swift action was necessary so that “impunity is decisively checked before January.” He spoke on Tuesday in Abuja at the Inspector General of Police’s Interactive Session with Chairmen and Secretaries of Political Parties on a peaceful electoral process before, during and after the 2027 General Elections. The session held at the Goodluck Ebele Jonathan Peace Conference Hall, Force Headquarters. He said the Electoral Act 2026 had “significantly strengthened legal deterrence,” adding that Sections 96 and 97 prohibit inciting campaign rhetoric and ban the use of thugs, private armed guards or masquerades at political rallies. According to him, the Act prescribes penalties of up to ₦5 million or twelve months’ imprisonment for individuals, and up to ₦10 million for political parties, on initial breaches. “Under Section 148, INEC is empowered to prosecute electoral offenders directly upon receipt of completed case files,” he said, explaining the Commission’s request for prompt transmission of the files by the Police. The INEC chairman stressed that the Commission remained distinct from security agencies. “INEC is not a security agency; it lacks both the constitutional mandate and operational capacity to maintain public order, arrest offenders, or provide armed security,” he said. He said Section 95 of the Electoral Act assigns the duty of securing political rallies to the Police. The Section also mandates the Commissioner of Police in each state and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) to provide adequate security for rallies and processions, with support from the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) and other federal security agencies. Amupitan reminded political parties that INEC Guidelines require them to notify the Commissioner of Police in writing of rally venues and times, and to submit the details to the Commission at least ten days in advance. He appealed to political leaders “to refrain from seeking political support by creating fear,” urging them instead to “earn public confidence through integrity and transparency.” The Chairman said the nation was at “a decisive moment” on its democratic calendar. The Presidential and National Assembly elections will hold in 53 days, on Saturday, January 16, 2027, across 176,846 polling units. nigeria.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA — The Labour Party (LP) in Abia State has denied any political alliance between Governor Alex Otti and Senator Orji Uzor Kalu, representing Abia North Senatorial District, ahead of the 2027 general elections. The party also urged Kalu to desist from what it described as attempts to impose a political coalition on it, insisting that it was not interested in any alliance with the All Progressives Congress (APC) or any other party for the Abia North senatorial seat. The state Publicity Secretary of the party, Emenike Iroegbu, stated this following the dismantling of a billboard bearing the portraits of Otti and Kalu in Arochukwu Local Government Area. Iroegbu said the billboard, titled ‘Coalition of Choice’, was intended to create the impression of a political alliance between the governor and the senator, insisting that no such arrangement existed. The billboard was reportedly dismantled over concerns that it could mislead the public and for allegedly failing to comply with statutory outdoor advertising regulations. The party condemned its erection, describing it as an attempt to misinform voters in Abia North. Iroegbu said, “We have made it categorically clear that the Labour Party in Abia State is neither in talks nor in any form of political coalition with the APC or any other political party. “The Labour Party in Abia State has no coalition with any party as regards Abia North Senatorial Seat, and it is wrong for individuals or groups to erect billboards misinforming our people about a coalition when there is none. “We call on Senator Orji Uzor Kalu to stop trying to force a coalition on the Labour Party. Our party is not interested in any coalition for the Abia North senatorial seat.” He further alleged that Kalu was seeking to associate himself politically with Governor Otti ahead of the 2027 elections, adding that the Labour Party would not allow the public to be misled. The party commended the Abia State Signages and Advertising Agency (ABSSAA) for removing the billboard, stressing that public communication materials must comply with relevant regulatory requirements. Iroegbu also disclosed that the party had a substantive senatorial candidate for Abia North, Chief David Onuoha Bourdex. The deployment was approved following an interview session at the commission’s corporate headquarters in Jabi, Abuja, presided over by a board member, Justice Paul Adamu Galumje (JSC, rtd), on behalf of the Chairman, DIG Hashimu Salihu Argungu (rtd). In a statement by the commission’s spokesperson, Torty Njoku, the PSC said the new commissioner was charged to demonstrate professionalism and neutrality in the discharge of his duties, particularly as the country prepares for the 2027 general elections. According to the statement, Adamu was also tasked with addressing the security challenges confronting Zamfara State and prioritising public safety. Before his new appointment, Adamu served as Area Commander, Jos Metro, Plateau State Command; Area Commander in Yobe State; Deputy Commissioner of Police, Criminal Investigation Department (CID), Plateau State; and Commissioner of Police, SERVICOM, at the Force Headquarters, Abuja. An alumnus of the University of Maiduguri, where he obtained a Bachelor of Science degree in Linguistics, Adamu joined the Nigeria Police Force on June 10, 1994, as a Cadet Assistant Superintendent of Police. The commission said the approval had been communicated to the Inspector-General of Police through a letter signed by its Secretary, Chief Onyemuche Nnamani. nigeria.title: US confirmed as host of 2028 Copa America
nigeria.description: The Copa America will be staged in the United States for a second successive edition in 2028 just ahead of the Los Angeles Olympics, organizers announced on Tuesday. CONMEBOL, the South American football confederation, and CONCACAF, the governing body for North America, agreed to conduct the 49th edition of the event at US venues from June 9 to July 9, 2028. The Los Angeles Olympics are scheduled for July 14-30 but the first pre-Olympic group-stage men’s soccer matches begin on July 10, only hours after the Copa final. The tournament will feature 16 teams, the 10 nations from South America plus six countries from North America that will qualify through the 2027 CONCACAF Gold Cup. The event was also played in the United States in 2016, the Copa America Centenario, and 2024 ahead of the USA co-hosting the World Cup earlier this year. “The CONMEBOL Copa America is much more than a tournament: it is part of our identity, our history, and the greatness of South American football,” CONMEBOL president Alejandro Dominguez said. “In 2028, we will once again bring that passion to the United States, reaffirming our historic partnership with CONCACAF and our shared commitment to continuing to drive the growth of football across the continent.” The host cities and other details will be announced later. “We’re pleased to join forces again to bring the CONMEBOL Copa America to our region in 2028,” said CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani. “We look forward to working alongside CONMEBOL, the host venues, and other key parties to organize a first-class tournament.” The post US confirmed as host of 2028 Copa America appeared first on Vanguard News .

nigeria.title: ADC to Tinubu: Resign or face impeachment over Kano judgment
nigeria.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has asked President Bola Tinubu to resign or face impeachment over allegations that he interfered in the Supreme Court’s 2023 Kano governorship election judgment in exchange for Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf’s defection to the All Progressives Congress (APC). The party said Yusuf’s recent BBC Hausa interview had raised serious questions about the independence of the judiciary, alleging that the President may have used his office to influence a judicial outcome for political advantage. In a statement by its National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, the ADC described the allegation as a grave breach of the President’s constitutional oath and urged the National Assembly to investigate the alleged arrangement. “No conduct can be more heinous on the part of a democratically elected President than to make the administration of justice an instrument of political bargaining. No betrayal of the presidential oath can be more profound than to pervert the cause of justice in pursuit of personal political advantage,” the party said. The ADC said Yusuf’s account suggested that the President had secured a favourable judgment from the Supreme Court in return for the governor’s defection to the APC. “In plain language, what Governor Yusuf was has admitted to was that the President of Nigeria, Bola Ahmed Tinubu, got the highest court in the land to award him justice in exchange for him decamping to APC. This a very grave allegation that undermines every principle regarding the rule of law, independence of the judiciary, and, indeed, the fight against corruption,” it said. The party called on the National Assembly to initiate impeachment proceedings against Tinubu and compel all parties to the alleged arrangement to provide evidence. It warned that the alleged interference, if established, would undermine confidence in the Supreme Court and send a damaging signal to international investors about the state of the rule of law in Nigeria. “The Supreme Court is not an extension of the APC national secretariat, and the President of Nigeria is not the proprietor of the Nigerian judiciary. With this revelation, the President has signalled to the rest of the world, including investors, that the rule of law is dead in Nigeria and that the Supreme Court of Nigeria is actually pliant to the political whims of the President. What a shame,” the ADC said. The opposition party challenged the National Assembly to demonstrate whether its allegiance was to the President or the Constitution, saying its response would test its willingness to hold the President accountable. business.title: Anchorage Digital Sets Up Asset Manager to Offer Bitcoin Yield to Clients
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Anchorage Digital Sets Up Asset Manager to Offer Bitcoin Yield to Clients Anchorage Digital, the first federally chartered crypto bank in the U.S., is moving into asset management with a new subsidiary that will offer custody clients a way to earn yield on their bitcoin. The unit, called 61st Parallel Asset Management, is expected to start operating by early December, CEO Nathan McCauley said in an interview to CoinDesk. Its first product will be a bitcoin-denominated fund, meaning returns are measured in BTC rather than dollars. The name nods to the city of Anchorage, Alaska, which sits at 61 degrees north latitude. “We have increasingly heard clients say they want to earn on top of the assets they hold at Anchorage — something that’s very common among the large financial institutions of the world,” McCauley said. Anchorage has filed a Form ADV, the disclosure document investment advisers use to register with the Securities and Exchange Commission or state regulators, or to report as exempt advisers. The form covers a firm’s ownership, business, assets under management, fees and conflicts of interest. As of Tuesday afternoon, the SEC’s public adviser database showed no record for 61st Parallel, so the filing’s details were not yet public. Paperwork dating back to summer The entity itself is not new. New York state records show that 61st Parallel Asset Management LLC, a Delaware company, registered to do business in New York on July 8, listing an office on Park Avenue South in Manhattan. Anchorage already lets clients earn on some holdings. Its website lists staking, which pays rewards for helping secure proof-of-stake networks, and a separate rewards product for eligible assets. Bitcoin runs on proof-of-work and cannot be staked natively. Anchorage has not said publicly how the fund will generate yield, what it will charge or which clients will qualify. Those details matter to bitcoin holders, because bitcoin pays no interest on its own. Common ways to earn on it include lending coins out, posting them as collateral or selling options against them, and each carries its own risk. Public companies have already tested some of those approaches. Trump Media disclosed this month that it had pledged about 73% of its bitcoin to an options program in which the counterparty can rehypothecate, or reuse, the coins. From custodian to full-service bank Founded in 2017, Anchorage received a national trust bank charter from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency in January 2021, the first crypto firm to win one. The OCC lifted a 2022 consent order over the bank’s anti-money laundering controls in August 2025. The bank no longer stands alone. Last December, the OCC granted conditional approvals to five more digital asset firms, including Circle, Ripple, BitGo, Paxos and Fidelity Digital Assets, to become national trust banks. entertainment.title: Beyond the Mini LED Label: What Should Define Good Mini LED Performance?
entertainment.description: The presence of Mini LED tells a shopper something important about the light source behind an LCD panel. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? entertainment.title: A Safari, a Beach & Easy Entry? 5 African Spots for Your Christmas Holiday
entertainment.description: Five African destinations Nigerian passport holders can visit visa-free or with visa on arrival this Christmas holiday. Image: AI-generated. The group chat has the concerts, the dinners and the Detty December link-ups covered. But has anyone planned the getaway? Beyond the usual Lagos parties and end-of-year outings, there is a whole continent waiting to be explored, with sun-soaked beaches, wildlife safaris, exciting food scenes and cities with plenty of stories to tell. You do not have to spend weeks navigating embassy appointments and visa applications to make it happen, either. Several African countries offer Nigerian passport holders visa-free entry or visas on arrival, making a festive-season escape much easier to plan. Whether you are travelling solo, gathering your friends, taking the family along or joining a curated travel group, here are five destinations worth considering for your Christmas holiday. Kenya Imagine spotting lions and giraffes against a city skyline before breakfast, then catching an evening flight or train straight to the coast for fresh seafood by the Indian Ocean. That contrast is what makes Kenya such a rewarding December escape. Nairobi gives you immediate access to wildlife at Nairobi National Park and the Giraffe Centre alongside lively restaurants and art spaces in Westlands and Karen, while longer itineraries open up classic game drives in the Maasai Mara, views of Mount Kilimanjaro in Amboseli, and warm beach days in Diani or Watamu. Nigerian citizens enjoy visa-free entry for short stays of up to 60 days without needing a paid eTA, leaving more room in your budget for safaris and coastal stays. Rwanda Not everyone wants their year-end holiday to feel like a non-stop sprint, and Rwanda is built for travellers who prefer scenery, clean air, and an unhurried pace. Days in Kigali easily revolve around specialty coffee shops, contemporary art at Inema Arts Center, and a sobering, essential visit to the Kigali Genocide Memorial before you head out into the countryside. From the capital, you can track chimpanzees and walk above the trees in Nyungwe Forest, go on wildlife drives in Akagera National Park, or spend quiet afternoons along the shores of Lake Kivu. With 30-day visa-free entry for Nigerian passport holders, getting there is straightforward from start to finish. Mauritius Sometimes a proper Christmas break calls for leaving mainland schedules behind altogether for turquoise lagoons, catamaran cruises, and mountain trails. entertainment.title: Esther Adeyanju: This International Men’s Day, Let’s Make Room for Men’s Vulnerability
entertainment.description: “Men are not wired to show emotions.” A male friend once said to me during an argument. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Society has an interesting checklist for measuring a man’s success. A good job, a house, a car, a wife, children and financial stability. Preferably, all achieved before a certain age. But if a man struggles to achieve all these, is his life any less meaningful? Surely, a man’s worth cannot be reduced to his bank balance, job title or ability to convince everyone that he has everything under control. There must be room for men who are still becoming. entertainment.description: La Roche-Posay concluded its first Living Lab experience in Nigeria, welcoming Nigerian stakeholders to its opening party and three-day programme, held from 4 to 6 November 2026 at Oasis by The Five Palm, Victoria Island, Lagos. Inspired by the original Living Lab concept in Paris, the experience brought the science, research and expertise behind skincare closer to Nigerian consumers and healthcare professionals. It marked the brand’s first Living Lab in the country, creating a platform for more accessible conversations around skin health, dermatological innovation and everyday skincare. The experience opened with an exclusive session for healthcare professionals and invited guests before welcoming members of the public over the following two days. Each day featured three expert-led sessions exploring the role of dermatology and scientific research in advancing skin health, the wider impact of skin conditions on everyday life, and the importance of understanding product safety, tolerance and efficacy. The sessions brought together healthcare professionals and representatives from across Nigeria’s dermatological beauty and skincare community, encouraging knowledge-sharing and stronger connections between science, expertise and consumer education. The Effaclar and Mela B3 spaces explored concerns including blemishes and hyperpigmentation, while the Cicaplast and Lipikar corners introduced visitors to approaches to caring for sensitive, damaged and dry skin. sports.description: Micah Ford #20 of the Stanford Cardinal looks on before a game against the Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets on Sept. 26, 2026 at Stanford Stadium in Palo Alto, Calif. (Matthew Huang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) Micah Ford has witnessed the lows of this Stanford football era. In November 2024, as a freshman, he watched from the California Memorial Stadium sideline as quarterback Fernando Mendoza went "98 yards with my boys" to lead an epic Big Game comeback, handing Stanford its first four-game losing streak against Cal since 2005. He was in the building four months later, when recently hired general manager Andrew Luck fired Troy Taylor, the head coach who had recruited him, citing the need for a "reset" after an investigation concluded that Taylor had bullied and belittled female staffers. Ford saw all of it. The 3-9 season in 2024. The 4-8 campaign a year ago. The slow start this season. He played for one head coach as a freshman (Taylor), then another as a sophomore (interim Frank Reich), and now another as a junior playing for first-year head coach Tavita Pritchard. Chaos and turmoil were all he knew. Midway through October, the feeling couldn't have been much better. The Cardinal were 2-4, and each blowout loss looked worse than the last. His team lost those games by a combined 172 points. Ford, the engine of the offense at running back, wasn't producing. But after that 58-7 loss to then-No. 6 Notre Dame on Oct. 10, something changed. Stanford, led by Ford's sudden emergence, became an unrecognizable football team. The first six games of Ford's season: 95 carries, 350 yards (3.7 yards per carry) and four rushing touchdowns. The last five: 108 carries, 701 yards (6.5 YPC) and nine rushing touchdowns. His yardage totals, including receptions, in each of those games were 231, 208, 120, 150 and 156. He's been the most consistent presence for an offense that desperately needed it under fourth-year running backs coach Malcolm Agnew. Ford's success directly led to Stanford's (6-5, 4-4 ACC) success. The Cardinal have won four of their last five games. They destroyed Cal 44-28 in Saturday's Big Game and earned bowl-game eligibility for the first time since 2018. Looking back, Ford can easily say it was all worth it. "To be at a program where, obviously, I didn't have success early, and then to see it gel into the program that we knew it could be," Ford said Saturday, "it's kind of just, like, I'm at a loss of words for it. "Honestly, there was no way we were leaving without that axe today," he added, after rushing for 151 yards and two touchdowns. "I don't know how long (it's been since) Stanford kept it two years in a row. It's probably been a little while." Ford is correct. The last time Stanford won consecutive games against Cal was in 2018, the last of a dominant nine-year Big Game run. Following that season, the Bears won five of six matchups from 2019-2024. sports.title: Paul Pierce Admits 2013 Trade Built Current Celtics Core
sports.description: Neville E. Guard-Imagn Images The Boston Celtics won the 2024 NBA title, but the foundation was laid when the franchise traded away its biggest star. Paul Pierce, the man who led the team to victory in 2008, says he has zero regrets about leaving in 2013. He knows the picks Boston received from that deal turned into the two players who finally brought the trophy back. The Trade That Changed Everything Back in 2013, the Brooklyn Nets were desperate and desperate teams make mistakes. They traded for Pierce and Kevin Garnett, giving up three unprotected first-round picks and a pick swap. The Nets project failed hard, and the assets Boston got in return became the keys to the kingdom. According to HITC , Pierce told the Amongst Legends podcast that the trade was handled with total transparency. He respected the process even though it meant leaving Boston. When the Nets finished with a 21-61 record in 2016, Boston used the number three overall pick to draft Jaylen Brown. The next year, the Celtics exercised their pick swap after Brooklyn had the worst record in the league. In the 2017 Draft, Danny Ainge traded down to let the Sixers select Markelle Fultz while the Lakers chose Lonzo Ball. Boston then swooped in to select Jayson Tatum with the third pick. Those two young stars led the team to a championship in 2024, defeating the Mavericks in the Finals. Pierce Owns The Legacy Many fans might think trading Pierce was a mistake, but he sees it differently now. He says the current success of the franchise rests on the foundation his departure created. A Look Back at California Roots Conner Henry, a native of Claremont, California, is part of that long history. He was selected by the Houston Rockets in the 1988 NBA Draft, but he had signed with Boston in 1987. His time with the team was short, lasting only until he was cut that fall. During his stay, Henry averaged 2.7 points per game. AOL.com notes that the Celtics have sought talent from nearly every U.S. state since their early days.

sports.title: Cleveland Guardians Add Lefty Starter on $17.5 Million Deal
sports.description: Oct 12, 2026; Milwaukee, Wisconsin, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Kris Bubic (40) throws a pitch against the Milwaukee Brewers during the fifth inning in game two of the NLCS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at American Family Field. Mandatory Credit: Michael McLoone-Imagn Images The Cleveland Guardians made their first significant free-agent addition of the winter on Tuesday, agreeing to terms with left-hander Kris Bubic on a one-year, $17.5 million contract, according to multiple reports. The deal, which is pending a physical, is the largest one-year guarantee in franchise history and gives Cleveland a familiar AL Central arm to bolster a rotation that already features Parker Messick and Gavin Williams. Bubic, 29, was a 2025 American League All-Star with the Royals, posting a career-best 2.55 ERA over 116⅓ innings that season. His 2026 campaign was far more limited. Elbow and shoulder issues sidelined him for much of the year; he finished with a 3.76 ERA across 55 innings split between Kansas City and the Dodgers after a deadline trade. When healthy, he has shown a five-pitch mix built around a rising four-seam fastball, a firm changeup, and a pair of breaking balls, along with a delivery that has historically generated soft contact and ground balls. For Cleveland, the signing fits a clear priority. The Guardians entered the offseason looking to add starting pitching depth after a season in which they were the only team in baseball to have four pitchers make at least 30 starts. Bubic is expected to slot into the middle of a group that also includes Messick (2026 AL Rookie of the Year and Cy Young finalist), Williams (AL strikeout leader), Tanner Bibee, and several depth options. Outside the Bubic agreement, Cleveland’s offseason activity has been quiet and roster-focused. At the non-tender deadline, they non-tendered utility man David Fry, agreed to deals with relievers Matt Festa and Colin Holderman plus outfielder Blake Perkins to avoid arbitration, and have signed minor-league free agents (including right-hander Jairo Iriarte and left-hander Antoine Kelly). They also added several players to the 40-man roster and claimed José Tena off waivers. With the collective bargaining agreement set to expire December 1, the remaining window for additional moves is short . Bubic gives the Guardians an upside left-handed starter on a prove-it deal while they evaluate further pitching or lineup needs.

sports.title: NFL Clears DK Metcalf Of Suspension After Sunday Ejection
sports.description: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images The National Football League has decided against suspending Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf after he was ejected during Sunday’s loss to the Philadelphia Eagles. This ruling comes despite Metcalf committing two unsportsmanlike conduct penalties that led to his removal from the game late in the third quarter. The league determined that a suspension was not warranted for the incident where Metcalf allegedly tried to poke Eagles cornerback Cooper DeJean in the eye. While the suspension is off the table, the league will still review the conduct to see if a fine is necessary. Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy addressed the situation during his Monday media availability, noting that he and Metcalf had spoken about the event. McCarthy described the conversations between the two as “productive” and stated that any further discipline from the team would be kept internal. “Life’s about learning situations,” McCarthy said. He also expressed his belief in second chances, noting that he would judge Metcalf based on their personal interactions rather than just the penalty flags. A History of Discipline This ejection marks the third time in his eight-season career that Metcalf has been thrown out of a game. The final two games of the 2025 regular season carry a suspension for the player due to behavior stemming from a physical altercation with a Lions fan in Detroit. The financial toll on the player has been significant, with his fines totaling a whopping $245,647 according to reports. This total excludes an extra $555,555 fine associated with the two-game suspension resulting from the Lions fan altercation. After Sunday’s game, Metcalf exited the locker room without talking to reporters, though he came back to speak with the media on Monday. ProFootballTalk states that he rejected claims he intended to poke Cooper DeJean in the eye. With just one catch on four targets for two yards before ejection, the 28-year-old receiver struggled to find his rhythm this season. In 10 games, the two-time Pro Bowler has secured 36 of his 74 targets, accumulating 434 yards and only two touchdowns. Looking Ahead to Denver Metcalf remains on the Steelers’ active roster as they prepare for their next matchup. The team has a short week to recover before hosting the Denver Broncos at Acrisure Stadium. The game is scheduled for Friday, Nov. 27, with kickoff set for 3 p.m. ET. RotoBaller indicates that Metcalf currently sits as the WR40 in half-PPR scoring.

sports.title: Dyson Daniels Proves The League Wrong On Value
sports.description: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images Dyson Daniels is the Atlanta Hawks’ most valuable player, not Jalen Johnson, because he drives wins without shooting. Soaring Down South reported that Daniels holds a staggering +18.0 on/off net rating to start the year. This number is the best on the team. The league thinks a shooter is needed to win. Daniels is changing that view with his defense and speed. He impacts winning in every way except shooting, which is a rare skill set. The Thompson twins are the only other players who succeed this way, but both are struggling this season. Amen Thompson has a -9.7 on/off rating with the Rockets, while Ausar sits at +2.2 with the Pistons. Daniels has surpassed both of them. A Deal That Saves The Hawks Money Daniels remains on a team-friendly deal of $25 million per year through the 2029-2030 season. He will have the 35th-highest salary in the league that year, making it the 23rd-lowest contract. Other players in his $20-30 million range include Damian Lillard, Herb Jones, and PJ Washington. Daniels is only 23 years old, one year younger than Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg. By the time his contract ends after the 2030 season, he will be 27 and entering his prime. The contract gives the Hawks an advantage over other teams.

sports.title: Mahomes And Reid Show Chiefs Pride Supports Kansas City Current
sports.description: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images The Kansas City Chiefs did not wait for a press release to show support for their city. Patrick Mahomes and Andy Reid made their stance clear on Sunday at Arrowhead Stadium. While the team prepared for a matchup against the Arizona Cardinals, the focus shifted to a family moment that celebrated a local soccer title. Mahomes, dressed in his full uniform, stopped to greet his wife and children. This act of love happened right before kickoff on a cold November afternoon. A Family Moment on the Sideline The video of the reunion spread fast across social media after the league shared it. Mahomes was already in his red No. 15 jersey when he walked over to the sideline. His children were bundled up in warm coats against the chill. One daughter wore a pale pink puffer coat while the other stood close. The quarterback bent down to wrap his arms around both kids for hugs and kisses. He then turned his attention to Brittany Mahomes, who wore a long black coat. She reached up to touch his face before they shared a kiss. The NFL posted the clip on X with a simple note about the moment. They wrote, “@PatrickMahomes getting some pregame love from his favorite people,” according to Sports Illustrated . Fans React to the Tribute Local fans saw the connection between the NFL champion and the NWSL champions immediately. Brittany Mahomes had already shared photos of the Kansas City Current winning their title. Her husband and the head coach supported her, and the community took notice. People watching the feed reacted with warm words about the scene. One person commented, “Okay that hug actually got me,” per Sports Illustrated. Another viewer simply said, “They are adorable.” A third fan summed up the feeling of the day by writing, “pregame with the family hits different.” These comments show how much the city cares about all its teams, not just one. The Chiefs have built a culture that values family and local pride in equal measure. Mahomes and Reid proved that point without saying a word during the game. The team won their match against Arizona with a final score of 34 to 7 on Sunday. Now the squad looks ahead to their next challenge on the road. The Kansas City Chiefs will play the Buffalo Bills on Thursday, Nov. 26, at 8:20 p.m.

sports.title: Lakers Target P.J. Washington To Strengthen Frontcourt
sports.description: David Richard-Imagn Images The Los Angeles Lakers are making moves to fix their frontcourt before the trade deadline arrives. General manager Rob Pelinka wants to shore up the team’s depth and add a reliable wing player. Reports indicate the club is targeting Dallas Mavericks forward P.J. Washington to fill a specific hole in their rotation. Heavy.com outlines a specific plan where Dallas sends Washington to Los Angeles in exchange for Jarred Vanderbilt, Jaden Hardy, and two future second-round picks. The Mavericks would receive the picks to add assets to their roster while clearing space for other players. This move would reunite Washington with Luka Doncic, his former teammate from Dallas. The Lakers see Washington as the missing piece to help their star trio dominate the playoffs. Why The Lakers Need Washington Los Angeles has struggled to find a consistent two-way player at the forward spot this season. The team needs someone who can guard top scorers and hit open shots without needing the ball. Heavy.com notes that Washington fits this exact profile. Washington is putting up solid numbers this year. While shooting 36.2% from three-point range, he averages 14.0 points, 6.7 rebounds, and 1.3 assists. Those stats show he can contribute immediately without disrupting the flow of the offense. The Lakers have been linked to him for a long time, but the salary cap makes it difficult. His $88 million contract is a big hurdle, yet the front office seems willing to take the risk. Backup Center Search Continues While chasing Washington, the Lakers are also looking for a backup center to play behind Walker Kessler. Marc Stein reported Sunday that the team is actively seeking help in the middle. “Lakers have been actively searching for another center to play behind Walker Kessler and general manager Rob Pelinka has all but promised that a move is forthcoming to address that need,” Stein wrote. The team has limited draft capital to use as leverage in these talks. One potential target is Mavericks center Moussa Cissé. Rookie guard Walter Clayton Jr. could be added to Dallas’s roster, which might require moving Cissé, and Stein noted that the Lakers have only three tradeable second‑round picks, highlighting their limited draft capital, though Los Angeles could trade Kevon Looney and a pick for Cissé despite the 24‑year‑old logging just 36 minutes this season. He is a gamble on upside rather than a sure thing. The Trade Deadline Approach Rob Pelinka has made it clear that the team plans to be active before the deadline. He spoke on Spectrum SportsNet about the need to fix issues the team has spotted. “We’ll be active at the trade deadline to shore up things that we see,” Pelinka said during a Spectrum SportsNet interview. The front office knows the roster has gaps that need filling if they want to challenge for a championship.

sports.title: Jiri Lehecka leads Czechs to Davis Cup quarter-final victory over 2022 winners Canada
sports.description: Czech No 1 Jiri Lehecka beat Felix Auger-Aliassime 7-6(4) 6-2 to seal a 2-0 quarter-final victory for Czechia over Canada in the Davis Cup . The world No 14’s victory ensured Czechia booked their place in the last four of tennis’ ‘World Cup’ for the first time in more than a decade. Earlier on Tuesday Tomas Mahac beat Liam Draxl 6-2 3-6 6-2 to put the Czechs in front, with Lehecka’s straightforward win meaning there was no need for the dead-rubber doubles match to be played, with Davis Cup ties best of three. Auger-Aliassime, a former world No 4 now ranked 17th, squandered ​nine ⁠break points, including a set ‌point at 5-4 in the opening set, before Lehecka forced a tiebreak. He continued to keep the Canadian under pressure with his aggressive play and powerful forehand, earning an early break before going 3-0 up in the second set, and converted his second match point before celebrating with his teammates. Lehecka said: “It was a super tough match. I was forced to play very well facing some break points and some tough situations. “Felix is such a dangerous player in these conditions, so I’m very proud with the way I converted the chances I had in the first set and also how I was able to improve my game in the second. I think it’s a great win, not just for me but for the whole team and I’m very, very proud of the team.” Earlier Machac, the mixed doubles champion from the 2024 Paris Olympics, made a flying start against world No 154 Draxl, surging into a 4-0 lead in ‌the first set. But what had looked like an easy win for the Czech turned into a real battle as Draxl fought back to force a decider. Machac regained control by breaking ‌for a 4-2 lead ​in the third before sealing ‌victory in an hour and 55 minutes.

sports.title: NFL Thanksgiving week games: Ranking the 5 weekday games by what's on the line
sports.description: The NFL went out of its way to schedule five compelling matchups for Thanksgiving Eve, Thanksgiving and Black Friday. The schedule comes out in May, and things can change dramatically over six months. Yet four of the five matchups have held up very well. That's not a bad percentage, even if the Eagles and Cowboys have let us down. Everyone will watch those two marquee franchises anyway. There's a lot on the line in terms of the playoff race during this week. We rank the most important games, in terms of what's at stake. 1. Chiefs at Bills We could look back on this game as the one that determined where the AFC championship game is played. The Bills lead the conference at 9-1, but the 8-2 Chiefs can pull even with a win and also clinch the head-to-head tiebreaker. The 8-2 Broncos also will have a big say in the race for the No. 1 seed, as could the Jaguars and Bengals who are each 7-3. sports.title: Orioles Spend Franchise-Record $125 Million in Deal for Pitcher
sports.description: Oct 26, 2026; St. Petersburg, Florida, USA; Tampa Bay Rays pitcher Freddy Peralta (51) looks on from the dugout after a pitching change against the Milwaukee Brewers during the fifth inning in game three of the 2026 World Series at Tropicana Field. Mandatory Credit: Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images Less than a day after watching left-hander Trevor Rogers depart for the Chicago Cubs on a five-year, $120 million contract, the Baltimore Orioles moved quickly to replace him. On Tuesday, the club agreed to terms with free-agent right-hander Freddy Peralta on a five-year, $125 million deal, according to multiple reports. The contract contains no opt-outs and no deferred money and remains pending a physical. The $25 million average annual value is the largest commitment the Orioles have ever made to a pitcher. Peralta, who turns 31 next June, becomes the clear front-of-the-rotation arm for a staff that already features Kyle Bradish and Shane Baz. Peralta’s path to Baltimore was circuitous. The Brewers traded him to the Mets last January with one year remaining on his contract. After posting a 4.99 ERA in 22 starts with New York, he was dealt to the Rays at the 2026 trade deadline. In Tampa Bay, he stabilized, going 5-2 with a 3.25 ERA across 10 starts and 55⅓ innings. He then elevated his profile in October, winning ALCS MVP honors after helping the Rays reach the World Series. In the postseason, he logged a 2.95 ERA over 21⅓ innings. For the full season, Peralta finished 10-11 with a 4.42 ERA in 169 innings. Career-wise, he is 80-53 with a 3.71 ERA and more than 1,300 strikeouts across parts of nine seasons, with two All-Star appearances on his résumé. Because he was traded midseason, he was ineligible for a qualifying offer and costs Baltimore no draft compensation. Outside the Peralta agreement, the Orioles’ free-agent activity this winter has been modest. They avoided arbitration with closer Félix Bautista on a one-year, $2.35 million deal and have signed several minor-league free agents (including infielder José Barrero and others). They also added multiple players to the 40-man roster ahead of the potential Rule 5 draft and claimed right-hander Braden Nett off waivers. The major-league rotation and lineup, however, had not received a significant free-agent infusion until Peralta’s deal. With the collective bargaining agreement set to expire on December 1 and a lockout widely expected, the window for further big-ticket moves is short. Baltimore still appears to be looking for additional pitching depth —particularly a left-hander—and could explore further roster upgrades before any work stoppage.

technology.title: How brewers can protect beers from smoke-tainted hops
technology.description: The 2020 Oregon wildfires burned over 1 million acres, destroyed thousands of structures, and killed 11 people. Smoke from the fires spread across the entire region; this "smoke taint" adversely affected not only local wine production , but also hops grown for beer brewing. Since the Pacific Northwest produces more than 95 percent of US hops and about 40 percent of the global supply, the potential economic impact is significant. That's why Oregon State University (OSU) scientists have been studying how brewers could offset the negative impacts of smoke taint while still incorporating affected hops in their brews. Most recently, they found that it all depends on the quantity of tainted hops that are included and when hops are added during the brewing process, according to a new paper published in the Journal of the American Society of Brewing Chemists. As previously reported , the chemistry of brewing beer is a very active area of research. For instance, in 2018 , OSU chemist Thomas Shellhammer—who also co-authored this latest paper— identified the growing popularity of " dry hopping " (adding hops after fermentation, common for pale ales) among craft brewers as the likely culprit of the exploding beer bottle phenomenon. science.title: 1st-ever detection of a dying star's 'final nuclear heartbeat' challenges what we know about our sun's eventual death
science.description: null As ubiquitous as the sun is to us today, our star is not eternal; one day, albeit in billions of years, it will die. While massive stars die in supernova explosions, the sun and stars of similar mass die quieter deaths. But that doesn't mean these stars completely go out with a whimper. New observations collected using the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA), the world's largest radio telescope comprised of 66 antennas in northern Chile, reveal that the sun's death throes may be different from what scientists had initially believed. NASA Jet Propulsion Lab (JPL) researcher Raghvendra Sahai, who led the investigation, explained the shape the ALMA observations took: "It's essentially a physical snapshot of an event that, until now, we've mostly inferred from theoretical models. We've caught, for the first time, a star's final nuclear heartbeat, frozen in gas." Sun-like stars "die" when they run out of hydrogen in their cores. This means that the fusion of hydrogen to helium ceases in the stellar core, and because this nuclear process is a star's main energy source, the star no longer has the outward push to support itself against the inward push of its own gravity. As the star's core collapses to create a stellar remnant called a white dwarf , the outer layers where hydrogen is still fusing to form helium swell out. This expansion leads to a relatively short-lived " red giant " phase. Eventually, these outer layers will cool and disperse, leaving the central white dwarf surrounded by a so-called "planetary nebula" shell of debris. During the red giant phase, as the stellar core is surrounded by shells of hydrogen and helium, these layers are occasionally rocked by flares in nuclear activity called thermal pulses. During these episodes, stellar material is flung into space. To better understand this phase in stellar evolution, the team focused ALMA on a star called IRAS 06530-0213, located around 12,000 light-years away in the constellation Monoceros. This revealed a giant ring of gas that appears to be a frozen fossil of the star's last thermonuclear flare-up. This thermonuclear fossil rings an hourglass-shaped planetary nebula in the act of forming. "Most of us think of stars as unchanging points of light, but this is a real-time snapshot of a star's death throes," Sahai said. "It's the brief, violent transition between a bloated red giant and a glowing planetary nebula, frozen mid-action." It represents the first direct evidence of the last thermal pulse before this kind of star enters the final phase of its life. science.title: Double asteroid solar eclipse caught on camera | Space photo of the day for Nov. 24, 2026
science.description: null (Image credit: ESA) A spacecraft far from Earth beamed home a rare sight: a solar eclipse caused by one asteroid casting its shadow on another. What is it? The image shows the Didymos double asteroid system , which consists of the larger Didymos and its moonlet, Dimorphos. In this image, Dimorphos' shadow can be seen on the surface of Didymos. The image was captured by the European Space Agency's (ESA's) Hera probe, which was sent to rendezvous with Didymos. Once there, Hera's job is to inspect the system to study the aftermath of NASA's historic DART mission (Double Asteroid Redirect Test), which slammed a kinetic impactor into Dimorphos in September 2022 in an attempt to alter its orbit and thus the trajectory of the entire two-asteroid system. Such missions, should they ever be needed in the future, could potentially redirect an asteroid on a collision course with Earth. Why is it incredible? For one, this image is incredible given that it was beamed home by Hera while it approaches Didymos some 121 million miles (195 million kilometers) away from Earth. But more than that, this image reveals incredible details of the Didymos system. Scientists call Didymos a "rubble pile" asteroid , meaning it's a loose body made up of boulders, dust, gravel and other bits of the solar system held together by the asteroid's own gravity. In the image, many of these irregular boulders and rocks can be seen strewn across Didymos and its moonlet. Hera will reach the system on Nov. 25, and ESA will release the first full images from the mission.

science.title: China launching 1st international astronaut to Tiangong space station today: Watch it live
science.description: null China will send an international astronaut to its Tiangong space station today (Nov. 24) for the first time ever, and you can watch the landmark liftoff live. A Long March 2F rocket is scheduled to launch the Shenzhou-24 mission from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China today at 7:18 p.m. EST (0018 GMT and 8:18 a.m. Beijing time on Nov. 25). You can watch the liftoff live here at Space.com, courtesy of China Central Television (CCTV). China rolls out the Long March 2F rocket for its Shenzhou-24 astronaut mission on Nov. 17, 2026. (Image credit: CCTV) Shenzhou-24 will be China's 18th crewed spaceflight to date and its 12th astronaut mission to Tiangong , a three-module station that the nation finished assembling in low Earth orbit in late 2022. Those numbers may sound rather prosaic. But today's flight will make history, marking the first time that China has ever launched a foreign national to space. That trailblazer is Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, a former pilot in Pakistan's armed forces who will be the first person from his country ever to reach orbit. (Adventurer Namira Salim is the first Pakistani ever to fly to the final frontier, doing so on a Virgin Galactic suborbital mission in October 2023 .) China and Pakistan began paving Ali's path to Tiangong in February 2025 , with the signing of a spaceflight cooperation agreement in Islamabad. Pakistan then selected two astronaut candidates, who traveled to China for training. We didn't learn which Pakistani astronaut was picked for Shenzhou-24 until Monday night (Nov. 23), when China announced the mission's crew. This is not out of the ordinary, by the way; China generally doesn't reveal the identity of Shenzhou astronauts until the day before launch. This is in keeping with the nation's broader spaceflight ethos, which prizes keeping things close to the vest. Ali is flying as a payload specialist. The other Shenzhou-24 astronauts are commander Tang Hongbo and flight engineer ​Wu Yi. Tang also flew on the Shenzhou-12 and Shenzhou-17 missions, which launched in June 2021 and October 2023, respectively. He will be the first person to visit Tiangong three times, according to the state-run Xinhua news agency. Shenzhou-24 will be the first spaceflight for Wu. Tang and Wu are expected to live aboard Tiangong for six months, the usual Shenzhou rotation. But Ali will stay in orbit for just a week or so, coming back down to Earth with Zhang Zhiyuan and Lai Ka-ying of the Shenzhou-23 mission, which launched on May 24 . According to the South China Morning Post, the third Shenzhou-23 crewmate, Zhu Yangzhu, will stay behind when Ali leaves, living aboard Tiangong until Shenzhou-24 comes home. Zhu will therefore become the first Chinese astronaut ever to spend a year in orbit, a milestone that will allow China to prep for long-duration missions to the moon and other deep-space locales.

science.title: Russia launches Progress 97 cargo ship to the International Space Station (video)
science.description: null Russia's latest freighter is on its way to the International Space Station. The robotic Progress 97 cargo craft launched atop a Soyuz rocket from the Russia-run Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan today (Nov. 24) at 5:17 a.m. EST (1013 GMT; 3:17 p.m. Baikonur time), carrying several tons of supplies for the astronauts aboard the orbiting lab. If all goes to plan, Progress 97 will arrive at the International Space Station (ISS) on Thursday (Nov. 26), docking with its Poisk module. But the freighter won't stay at that particular locale for long. A Russian Soyuz rocket launches the uncrewed Progress 97 cargo ship to the International Space Station from Baikonur Cosmodrome, Kazakhstan on Nov. 24, 2026. (Image credit: NASA) The cosmonauts currently living on the ISS — Pyotr Dubrov, Anna Kikina and Sergey Teteryatnikov — will unload Progress 97 through Poisk. But the freighter will then hop over to a different port, according to journalist and space historian Anatoly Zak: the aft one of the PrK transfer tunnel, which leads to Russia's Zvezda service module. The PrK port is the best site for engine burns that boost the orbit of the ISS, a service that Progress freighters regularly provide. But Progress 97 cannot unload its cargo through that port because the PrK transfer tunnel has been sealed off, due to an ongoing air leak that was first documented in 2019. Progress-97 is therefore "the first cargo mission scheduled to unload its cargo and perform orbit corrections of the ISS at different docking ports," Zak wrote on the site he runs, RussianSpaceWeb.com. Progress 96 cargo spacecraft packed with science and supplies approaches the International Space Station for a docking on Sept. 19, 2026. (Image credit: NASA) The Progress 97 mission, which Russia calls Progress MS-36, was originally expected to launch this past August, according to Zak. But the liftoff was pushed back several times, most significantly by the collapse of the service platform at Baikonur's Site 31 in November 2025. It took Russia about three months to repair the platform, leading to a series of delays. Progress 97 will likely stay docked to the ISS for about six months, after which it will be loaded up with trash and sent home to burn up in Earth's atmosphere . Japan's HTV-X vehicle and Northrop Grumman's Cygnus spacecraft are similarly expendable. The only currently operational ISS cargo craft that's reusable is SpaceX's Dragon capsule, which makes parachute-aided ocean splashdowns at the end of its missions.
